title: Online posts targeting Singapore's Indian community and the Government's response
asked: Mr Darryl David asked whether investigations showed the 14 posts targeting the Indian community were a coordinated effort by any agency or organisation, and what action has been or will be taken against such a body. Dr Neo Kok Beng asked whether the national framework and tools will be reviewed, and what programmes will equip residents to discern negative external influences.
asked_by: Mr Darryl David and Dr Neo Kok Beng
response: Mr Goh Pei Ming said there is currently no evidence of a coordinated campaign by any particular government or organisation, and that investigations showed the content likely originated from a China-based platform before being carried on other platforms. The posts were assessed to fall under section 298A(a) of the Penal Code, and Disabling Directions under the Online Criminal Harms Act were issued to block Singapore users' access to the 14 posts. He said the Government monitors the infospace closely, reviews its laws regularly, and set out public-education efforts including National Education and Total Defence, the SG101 website, NLB's S.U.R.E. programme, briefings and workshops, and a 2025 MHA campaign on deepfake and AI-generated content.

key_points.point: No evidence was found of a coordinated campaign by any particular government or organisation.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: There is currently no evidence to suggest that this is a coordinated campaign by any particular government or organisation.

key_points.point: Investigations indicated the content likely came from a China-based platform and was then carried on other platforms and websites.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: Investigations revealed that the content likely originated from a China-based platform

key_points.point: The content was assessed to be an offence under section 298A(a) of the Penal Code for promoting ill-will between racial groups.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: knowingly promoting feelings of enmity, hatred or ill-will between different groups on grounds of race

key_points.point: Disabling Directions under the Online Criminal Harms Act were issued to block Singapore users' access to the 14 posts.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: The Government has issued Disabling Directions under the Online Criminal Harms Act (OCHA) to block access by Singapore users to the 14 online social media posts.

key_points.point: The SG101 website consolidates government educational resources on foreign interference and Singapore's positions on sensitive issues.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: The SG101 website is a one-stop Government site that consolidates educational resources on foreign interference

key_points.point: The National Library Board runs the S.U.R.E. programme to build critical reading and fact-checking skills.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: The National Library Board works to cultivate critical reading as a foundational skill

key_points.point: MHA ran a 2025 campaign on deepfake videos and AI-generated content used to influence overseas jurisdictions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: The Ministry of Home Affairs also rolled out a campaign in 2025 on the use of deepfake videos

key_points.point: Online directions under FICA were first used in July 2024.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: Our online directions under FICA were first issued or first used in July 2024.

key_points.point: The directions have been generally effective, with social media companies complying.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: They have been generally effective as the social media companies have worked with us and complied with the directions issued by the Government.

key_points.point: The number of such posts is rising, and every case is tracked, including possible state actors behind them.
key_points.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
key_points.quote: we do see an increase and we do track very carefully every single case

left_open: What action would be taken against a specific agency or organisation, given that no such organisation was identified in this case.
How the effectiveness of the preventive and legislative measures is measured.
supplementary: Whether such cases are tracked and rising, and whether Singapore's laws are proactive or reactive and how their effectiveness is measured.
